findings.text: Device page range initializer prepares a power of two span at a base page for a supplied device mapping and order, associating each member with that mapping and resetting per folio state, then acquires a reference on the mapping, establishes a count on the head, locks the head, and finalizes compound state when ordered.

Device initialization expects an order within the maximum allocation order, expects cleared prior compound order and head markings on every member, expects no preexisting references and expects zone device identity already established for each folio before the final reference and lock are taken.

Early boot memory test entry iterates a configured number of passes over a physical interval, cycling backwards through a fixed pattern table, and delegates each pass to a free range walker that clamps ranges and tests only the overlapping portion.

Memory test pattern table begins with a zero entry so a completed run leaves memory zeroed, test count zero disables all testing, and a reporting helper emits nothing unless boot testing ran and proc style reporting is enabled, rounding any nonzero sub kilobyte bad total up to one kilobyte.

Single pattern test aligns the start upward, writes the pattern across the addressable span, then rereads sequentially, coalescing physically contiguous mismatches into one bad interval per gap and reserving each completed interval before starting the next, with a trailing reservation after the scan.

Migration statistics record carries separate tallies for base page success and failure plus distinct counters for transparent huge page success, failure, splitting, and a broader large folio split count, with failure accounting excluding folios never attempted.
Reverse map walk argument bundles a target folio pointer with a boolean that enables replacement of unused zero filled subpages by the shared zero page during migration entry removal.
Overall page migration retry ceiling is ten passes with an asynchronous sub ceiling of three, leaving the synchronous remainder derived as their difference.
Batched migration capacity has two build dependent forms, one tied to the number of base pages in a PMD mapped huge page and an alternate fixed numeric capacity of several hundred.
Migration history flags use two distinct low bit positions for previously mapped and previously locked states, with a combined mask representing both old states together.

Buffer folio migration holds no folio private lock while acquiring each buffer head around the circular list, using nonblocking attempts in asynchronous mode and limited blocking in light synchronous mode, releasing all already held buffers on failure to avoid partial hold.

Reference checked buffer migration serializes the busy check with a dedicated migrate bit on the head buffer plus the address space private spinlock while inspecting per buffer use counts, with one LRU invalidation and recheck before reporting busy, and always clears the bit and releases buffers on exit.

Huge page mapping transfer performs reference freeze and page cache replacement while holding the address space iterator lock in interrupt disabled mode, unlocking on freeze failure and only updating index, mapping, references and cache entry while frozen.

User page move and status paths hold the address space read lock during virtual area lookup and folio walk, and the bulk move path additionally disables LRU caching across the whole batch, reenabling it on every exit path including early faults.

Zero page substitution during migration applies only to anonymous locked non compound non poisoned subpages whose old entry is not present, rejects locked folios and locked areas and address spaces that forbid the zero page, rejects device private folios, and requires content identical to the shared zero page.

Migration entry removal walks each mapping, delegates PMD mapped huge entries to a separate helper, derives a subpage index for large non hugetlb folios from entry offset, optionally substitutes zero pages, then rebuilds a present entry preserving age, dirtiness, soft dirtiness, writability, userfault handling and exclusivity before installing it with appropriate reverse map accounting and cache update.

Anonymous hugetlb reverse map addition requires hugetlb and anonymous identity, increments both entire and large mapping tallies, conditionally marks exclusivity, and warns if exclusivity is claimed while more than one entire mapping exists.

Folio migration helpers expose file backed transfer, buffered transfer without extra reference validation, buffered transfer with reference validation, and a hugetlb mapping transfer that validates expected references, copies content, then atomically swaps cache presence.

Migration target allocator resolves a default node from the source when none is specified, routes hugetlb sources through a hugetlb allocator with adjusted mask and fallback policy, adjusts reclaim and huge allocation flags plus order for large folios, preserves high memory and movable zone placement, then allocates the destination folio.

Bulk user page move groups consecutive requests by target node, queues isolated folios per group, flushes each completed group to the destination and records per page status, treats lookup and isolation failures as per page status rather than aborts, and accounts unattempted pages when aborting after failures.

Move and status paths reject shared zero folios and huge zero folios and zone device folios with distinct errors, skip folios already on the target node, reject shared mapped folios unless an all shared flag is set, and validate target node range, memory state and task allowed mask before queuing.

Boot memory report helper formats the accumulated reserved bad byte total as kilobytes in a single labeled line after successful testing, while the boot parser interprets an optional numeric argument as a test count and defaults to the full pattern table length when absent.

Early memory testing destructively overwrites free physical ranges and permanently reserves failing intervals, so running it outside early initialization or over live memory risks data loss and unexpected reservation growth.

Device page initialization warns when the order exceeds limits, when folios carry references, when identity is not zone device, and when the device mapping reference cannot be acquired, indicating reuse after unmap or concurrent allocation misuse.

Migration helpers return a transient retry signal when reference counts exceed the expected isolated value, when buffer locks cannot be obtained without stalling, when buffers remain busy after invalidation, and when content copy reports an error, requiring callers to handle partial progress and retries.
